verses.text: Then the LORD spoke to me.
“Don’t get married here, and don’t have sons or daughters in this place.”
Here’s what the LORD says about the sons and daughters born here, the mothers who gave birth to them, and the fathers who had them in this land:

“They’ll die terrible deaths. Nobody will mourn them or bury them. They’ll lie on the ground like manure. The sword and famine will finish them off. Their bodies will be food for birds and wild animals.”

The LORD says, “Don’t go into a house where people are mourning. Don’t go to grieve or cry for them. I’ve taken my peace away from these people,” says the LORD, “along with my faithful love and tender mercy.
The powerful and the powerless will both die in this land. Nobody will bury them. Nobody will mourn for them, cut themselves for them, or shave their heads for them.
Nobody will break bread for the mourners to comfort them over someone who died. Nobody will offer them a cup of comfort over the loss of a father or mother.
“Don’t go into a house where people are feasting to sit down and eat or drink with them.”
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “Right in front of your eyes, in your lifetime, I’ll silence the sounds of celebration and joy here. You won’t hear the voices of a bride or groom.
When you tell these people all this, they’ll ask, ‘Why has the LORD declared such a huge disaster against us? What did we do wrong? What sin did we commit against the LORD our God?’
Tell them, ‘Your ancestors walked away from me,’ says the LORD. ‘They chased other gods, served them, and worshiped them. They left me and didn’t keep my law.
You’ve done even worse than your ancestors. Every one of you follows your own stubborn, evil heart, so you won’t listen to me.
So I’ll throw you out of this land into a land you and your ancestors have never known. You’ll serve other gods there day and night, because I won’t show you any favor.’
“So look, the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when people won’t say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, the one who brought the children of Israel out of Egypt.’

They’ll say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, the one who brought the children of Israel back from the land up north and from all the countries where he drove them.’ I’ll bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors.

“Look, I’ll call in a crowd of fishermen,” says the LORD, “and they’ll fish these people out. Then I’ll send for plenty of hunters, and they’ll hunt them down from every mountain and hill and out of every crack in the rocks.
I’ve got my eyes on everything they do. They can’t hide from me, and their wrongdoing isn’t out of my sight.
First I’ll pay them back double for their wrongdoing and sin. They’ve polluted my land with the carcasses of their disgusting things and filled my inheritance with what I can’t stand.”

LORD, you’re my strength, my fortress, and my safe place when trouble comes. Nations will come to you from the ends of the earth and say, “Our ancestors inherited nothing but lies, empty things that never did anybody any good.
Should people make gods for themselves when those things aren’t even gods?”
“So watch. This time I’ll make sure they know my hand and my power. Then they’ll know that my name is the LORD.”
